thread:
Maya: IncidentBot alerted: sustained p99 spikes on /streaming/generate across us-west-2, started ~03:12UTC. Observed streaming stalls + partial responses.
IncidentBot: [AUTOMATED] Incident created: INC-1829004322. Sev=high. Playbook: kv-cache-paging-prefill.
Linus: seeing corresponding jump in kv-prefill eviction_rate on shard-42, eviction tail latency also increased. prefill vs decode ratio skewed ~6:1.
Maya: confirmed. p95 moved from 120ms -> 450ms; p99 from 320ms -> 1.6s on impacted nodes. Streaming stall count up 8x.
SRE_Jam: logs show repeated slab-alloc retries and `KV_EVICT_FAST` events. Could be fragmentation + one noisy workspace. Querying top tenants now.
Emily: here's the quick metric query I ran: 
```
sum(rate(kv_prefill_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard)
```
shard-42 is 4.1x baseline. Also prefill_bytes_out is spiking.
Patrick: noisy tenant id 3512 has a storm of long-context requests (avg seq_len 14000). They're hitting prefill path heavily. Possibly prefill queue backpressure causing decode to wait -> streaming stalls.
Linus: routing policy note: for long-context we prefill aggressively which can fragment slabs. If a single tenant monopolizes prefill it evicts useful decode cache.
Maya: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) throttle prefill requests for tenant 3512 by rate-limiting on the edge, 2) lower prefill concurrency on shard-42, 3) enable emergency fallback routing to smaller-ctx model for that tenant. Thoughts?
SRE_Jam: do 1 + 2 asap. Fallback (3) requires product ok but can be done as a temporary routing rule. I'll prepare patch for slab-reshard hint but that's medium-term.
Emily: +1 on throttling. Command to enact edge rate-limit (approx): 
```
# temp rate-limit tenant 3512 to 3r/s
curl -X POST "https://edge-control/api/rl" -d '{"tenant":3512,"qps":3,"reason":"incident-1829004322"}'
```
Maya: executing now. Applying prefill concurrency cap on shard-42 to 4 (was 12). Pushing config...
IncidentBot: Action logged: edge rate-limit applied for tenant 3512 by Maya at 03:20UTC.
Linus: after cap, eviction_rate dropped ~60% within 90s. p95 back down to ~160ms, p99 trending down. Streaming stalls reduced but not fully resolved.
Patrick: we still see decode queue depth spikes — looks like cache miss rate increased for decode path due to prior evictions. Need time for useful KV to rebuild.
Maya: enabling short-circuit fallback: route tenant 3512 to smaller-ctx model (gpt-small) for next 15m to reduce memory pressure. Notifying product.
Emily: routing change pushed. Monitoring.
SRE_Jam: note for on-call: consider gradual slab shrink rollback after pressure normalizes. Also plan a tenant-level mitigation doc so we can flip quiesce flags faster next time.
Linus: customer impact: a subset of streaming sessions saw partial responses and increased latencies. ETA for full recovery ~12-18m given cold cache rebuild.
Maya: handoff to night oncall @Linus in 30m. Will include runbook steps: 1) monitor p99/p95, 2) check eviction_rate, 3) if eviction_rate > 2x baseline reapply throttles, 4) consider model fallback if decode saturation persists.
Patrick: collecting logs for postmortem: saving `kv_eviction_*`, `streaming_tail_*`, `prefill_queue_*` for window 03:05-03:40.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-1829004322 updated: mitigations applied, customer throttled, fallback enabled. Next update required in 15m or on status change.
Emily: preliminary RCA notes: root cause = heavy long-context tenant load causing prefill-dominant traffic -> fragmenting KV slabs -> eviction storms -> decode path cache misses -> streaming tail stalls. Contributing factor: no prefill prioritization per-tenant.
Maya: agreed. Post-incident actions (put into ticket): - tenant-specific prefill backpressure controls - soft isolation for prefill heavy tenants - improve eviction telemetry to surface tenant attribution - add adaptive prefill concurrency knob tied to slab pressure.
Linus: will take lead on telemetry and tenant attribution item. Patrick on runbook improvements. Emily on emergency routing docs.
Maya: handoff: Linus you own post-incident fixes and next 24h monitoring. I'll update incident channel and ping affected account team.
Linus: taking handoff. continuing watch. ping me for escalations. :thumbsup:
Patrick: saving all logs to s3://redwood-incidents/1829004322/ for later analysis.
Maya: closing active mitigations after 25m once metrics stable. Thanks team.
